passages.text: Simon said, “How, then, when the maker was known—the one who formed Adam and was known to the righteous according to the law, and furthermore to the righteous and unrighteous and the whole world—does your teacher, coming after all those people, say, ‘No one knew the Father except the Son, just as no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him’? He would not have said these things unless he were announcing a certain Father who is in secrecy, whom the law also calls Most High, from whom no good or evil utterance has been heard, as Jeremiah too testifies in the Lamentations. In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, who are seventy, and marking out the nations’ boundaries by seventy languages, this one gave the Hebrews as a portion to his Son, who is also called Lord and ordered heaven and earth, and appointed him God of gods. By gods I mean those who have received the other portions of the nations. Laws therefore issued from all the gods just mentioned to their own portions, namely the remaining nations; likewise the law established among the Hebrews issued from the Son, the Lord of all. It was determined to be this way so that if someone takes refuge in someone’s law, he becomes part of the portion of the one whose law he has undertaken to practice. No one knew the Most High Father who is in secrecy, just as no one knew of this one’s Son that he is Son. Indeed, you, assigning to the Son the distinctive attributes of the secret Most High, do not know that he is Son, being Father of the Jesus whom you call Messiah.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν ἀπορρήτοις
lexical_decisions.chosen: in secrecy
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression can mean among unrevealed mysteries or in the secret realm. In secrecy preserves the hidden status without inventing a named location.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κατὰ ἀριθμὸν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ
lexical_decisions.chosen: In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Israel, not another textual witness’s sons of God or angels; the explicit count seventy remains.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ αὐτοῦ υἱῷ τῷ καὶ „κυρίῳ“ λεγομένῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: to his Son, who is also called Lord
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Simon’s distinction between the Most High and his Son, who is the maker in this proposal, not the translator’s own theological identification.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ καθ’ ὑμᾶς λεγομένου χριστοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: the Jesus whom you call Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: χριστός is a disputed independent title attributed by Simon to the other party’s Jesus, so Messiah preserves the title’s force.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅστις κατὰ ἀριθμὸν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, οἳ εἰσῆλθον εἰς Αἴγυπτον (οἵ εἰσιν ἑβδομήκοντα), καὶ πρὸς τὰ ὅρια τῶν ἐθνῶν περιγράψας γλώσσαις ἑβδομήκοντα
lexical_decisions.chosen: In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, who are seventy, and marking out the nations’ boundaries by seventy languages
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object of περιγράψας is implicit. The English takes the boundaries named in πρὸς τὰ ὅρια as the contextual object of marking out, not as a direct Greek accusative object outside the preposition. A more formally separated alternative is having marked out divisions by seventy languages in accordance with that number and in relation to the nations’ boundaries. Both number and boundary expressions constrain the delineation; no additional printed noun is claimed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ πάντων κυρίου
lexical_decisions.chosen: from the Son, the Lord of all
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes the second genitive phrase appositionally, since the Son was already explicitly called Lord in this proposal. From the Son of the Lord of all is a material alternative attaching the second genitive as the Son’s parent; the main text does not claim the appositional grouping is uniquely settled.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν ἐν ἀπορρήτοις ὕψιστον πατέρα ὄντα, ὡς οὐδὲ τὸν τούτου υἱὸν ὅτι υἱός ἐστιν.
lexical_decisions.chosen: No one knew the Most High Father who is in secrecy, just as no one knew of this one’s Son that he is Son.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text reads Father attributively as the identification of the hidden Most High, whose inaccessible status and unheard voice Simon has described. A material alternative takes πατέρα ὄντα predicatively: No one knew that the Most High who is in secrecy is Father, just as no one knew that his Son is Son. That alternative aligns the two clauses as failures to recognize paternal and filial identity rather than knowledge of a person; the main reading is retained contextually, not claimed as unique.

passages.text: Peter said, “Since you have spoken in this way to please the crowds present, I will speak not to please them, but truthfully. Tell me: how do you know that everyone present is worthy, when not even one agreed with you as you disclosed it? For their praising me against you is not the act of people agreeing with you, but with me, to whom they also assigned praise as someone who had spoken rightly. But since God, being just, judges each person’s mind, he would not have wished what you say is true to be given to those on the right through the left. By the same reasoning, someone who receives anything from a thief is himself liable. Therefore, for this reason, he did not wish them to receive what you bring, but rather through the Son appointed to reveal. For who can reasonably reveal the Father except the Son alone, since he knows who is worthy of such revelation? Thus this cannot be taught or learned by teaching, but must be revealed by an inexpressible hand to the one worthy to know it.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: διὰ τῆς ἀριστερᾶς τοῖς δεξιοῖς
lexical_decisions.chosen: to those on the right through the left
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the right/left opposition without identifying unprinted named camps or persons.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀφράστῳ χειρὶ
lexical_decisions.chosen: by an inexpressible hand
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the hand image, not merely a generic divine act.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τίνι γὰρ εὔλογόν ἐστιν ἀποκαλύπτειν τὸν πατέρα ἢ υἱῷ μόνῳ διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι τῆς τοιαύτης ἀποκαλύψεως τὸν ἄξιον;
lexical_decisions.chosen: For who can reasonably reveal the Father except the Son alone, since he knows who is worthy of such revelation?
lexical_decisions.rationale: τίνι and υἱῷ identify the person for whom revealing is appropriate, thus the revealer. The Son’s preceding appointment and knowledge of worthy recipients confirm this role. The English does not make him the recipient by saying to whom the Father is revealed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀλλ’ ἐπειδὴ ὁ θεὸς δίκαιος ὢν βραβεύει τὸν ἑκάστου νοῦν, ὃ φῆς ἀληθὲς εἶναι, οὐκ ἂν ἐβουλήθη διὰ τῆς ἀριστερᾶς τοῖς δεξιοῖς τοῦτο δοθῆναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: But since God, being just, judges each person’s mind, he would not have wished what you say is true to be given to those on the right through the left.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes ὃ φῆς ἀληθὲς εἶναι as a fronted relative resumed by τοῦτο: the purported truth Simon brings. The subsequent what is brought by you supports this attachment. Alternatively it is parenthetical, which you say is true, modifying the claim that God judges each mind. The printed commas allow both; the revised main text prefers the resumed object without changing the Greek.

passages.text: Peter said, “I will answer what you want, concerning ‘No one knew the Father except the Son, nor does anyone know the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.’ First, I am amazed how, when this statement has countless interpretations, you chose the more dangerous part, saying that the statement referred to ignorance on the part of the maker and everyone made by him. For in the first place the statement can have been addressed to all the Jews who supposed David to be the Messiah’s father—with the Messiah himself being the son—and had not recognized him as Son of God. Therefore it was appropriately said, ‘No one knew the Father,’ since everyone named David instead of God. He added, ‘Nor does anyone know the Son,’ because they did not know that he was Son. Saying, ‘Those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him,’ was also rightly said, for the Son who has existed from the beginning alone was appointed to reveal to those he wishes. Thus Adam, the first formed, can have been not ignorant of him; nor can Enoch, who pleased him, fail to know; nor can righteous Noah fail to understand; nor can Abraham the friend fail to comprehend; nor can Isaac have failed to understand; nor can Jacob who wrestled have failed to believe; nor can he have remained unrevealed to all the worthy among the people.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ ἐπικινδυνότερον ἐξελέξω μέρος
lexical_decisions.chosen: you chose the more dangerous part
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the comparative, not the unsupported superlative most dangerous.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς ἀγνωσίαν τοῦ δημιουργοῦ καὶ τῶν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ πάντων
lexical_decisions.chosen: ignorance on the part of the maker and everyone made by him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitives are taken as subjective: maker and created ones are ignorant of the secret Father, as in Simon’s argument. Ignorance of the maker is an objective-genitive alternative, but fits the immediately preceding exchange less well.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῷ λαῷ ἀξίοις μὴ ἀποκεκαλύφθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor can he have remained unrevealed to all the worthy among the people
lexical_decisions.rationale: The final clause is read under the negative modal scope carried from the preceding οὐχ ... μὴ clauses. Its μὴ is retained in unrevealed and the carried denial in nor can. A clause-local reading, and not to have been revealed, remains possible but is less consonant with the preceding argument.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς πατέρα νομίζοντας εἶναι χριστοῦ τὸν Δαυὶδ — καὶ αὐτὸν δὲ τὸν χριστὸν υἱὸν ὄντα — καὶ υἱὸν θεοῦ μὴ ἐγνωκέναι.
lexical_decisions.chosen: who supposed David to be the Messiah’s father—with the Messiah himself being the son—and had not recognized him as Son of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The printed parenthesis is kept outside the failure-to-recognize phrase and can continue the supposed Davidic father-son relation. It could instead affirm the Messiah’s sonship parenthetically. A broader attachment, taking their failure as not recognizing him as Son and as Son of God, is a material alternative, but the parenthetical punctuation favors keeping the explicit Son-of-God denial as the failed recognition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδὲ Ἐνὼχ ὁ εὐαρεστήσας μὴ εἰδέναι οὔτε Νῶε ὁ δίκαιος μὴ ἐπίστασθαι οὔτε Ἀβραὰμ ὁ φίλος μὴ συνιέναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor can Enoch ... fail to know; nor can righteous Noah fail to understand; nor can Abraham ... fail to comprehend
lexical_decisions.rationale: The governing δύναται is carried through the list, with οὐδέ/οὔτε denying the modal possibility of each negative-infinitive failure. This gives the explicit nor can ... fail construction. Another reading coordinates the negative infinitival complements under a positive possibility—can be not ignorant, can be not without knowledge—without the same emphasis on exclusion of ignorance. The first Adam clause has only the negative infinitive and is kept as a positive possibility of nonignorance; the later coordinated negatives are made explicit rather than flattened.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδὲ τὸν υἱόν τις οἶδεν, εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor does anyone know the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object of reveal is unexpressed in Greek. In both quotation occurrences the English him supplies the Father, chosen from the surrounding discussion of the Son revealing the Father, including 18.10. The placement after the exception about knowing the Son also permits the Son or knowledge of his identity as the object of revelation. The Father is therefore an explicitly disclosed contextual choice, not a uniquely printed object; the quotation is not rearranged to match another witness.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῷ λαῷ ἀξίοις μὴ ἀποκεκαλύφθαι
source_issues.issue: The final coordination has μὴ but no newly repeated οὐχ. The English carries the previous negative modal scope, nor can ... unrevealed, rather than adding a new printed negation. A clause-local reading would instead yield and not revealed. The modal/negative scope across the entire list is explained in the lexical note on Enoch, Noah, and Abraham.

passages.text: But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him, how do you not call it most unjust that those men did not know him—seven pillars of the world who were able to please the most just God—while now so many from the nations, impious in every way, know him? Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all? And how is what is not just good? Unless by good you wish to mean not the one who benefits those who have acted justly, but the one who loves the unrighteous even if they do not believe, revealing to them also the secrets that he was unwilling to reveal to the righteous. Such conduct belongs neither to a good nor to a just being, but to one who hates the reverent. Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon, who dares to say these things, which have never been spoken in this way?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἑπτὰ στύλους ὑπάρξαντας κόσμῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: seven pillars of the world
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the stated seven without supplying an unprinted list of names.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μήτι σὺ εἶ, Σίμων, ὁ ἑστώς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the standing epithet and interrogative challenge, not a translator’s identification of Simon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δὲ (ὡς φῄς) ἔσται διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ νῦν πᾶσιν ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι:
lexical_decisions.chosen: But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Is to be retains future ἔσται while now retains νῦν. The main text construes διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι purposively, for the sake of knowing, with him supplied as the contextual object, the previously discussed Father. The causal alternative is because of knowing; the clause does not state whose prior knowledge would ground disclosure on that attachment. No claim is added that the revealed one was already known to everyone.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὗτοι παντὸς κρείττονος γνῶναι οὐ κατηξιώθησαν;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context concerns knowing the proposed highest Father, favoring a personal referent superior to all and παντός as the comparison of κρείττονος. Taking παντός with substantival κρείττονος gives the broader alternative Were these not deemed worthy to know anything superior? The genitive superior object is construed with deemed worthy/knowing in this compressed phrase; the personal interpretation is not claimed as unique.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μήτι σὺ εἶ, Σίμων, ὁ ἑστώς, ὁ ταῦτα οὕτως μήποτε ῥηθέντα εἰπεῖν ἀποθρασυνόμενος;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon, who dares to say these things, which have never been spoken in this way?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The things never spoken in this way are the object of Simon’s audacious saying. The phrase does not state that Simon himself claims they were previously spoken; the English does not introduce that unsupported reported-speech proposition.
